item.title: Intensity limits for phase-only holographic optical-tweezer arrays
item.description: arXiv:2611.10302v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Optical tweezers use tightly focused laser beams to trap and manipulate individual particles, enabling advances in quantum computing, drug discovery, and biological research. Scaling these technologies to large arrays requires delivering sufficient light to every trapping site while minimizing the total laser power required. Here, we investigate the fundamental limits of how efficiently a phase-only hologram can distribute light across an array of optical traps. We derive upper bounds on the minimum intensity across trapping sites, accounting for illumination, target geometry, and diffraction from spatial light modulator pixels. For arrays arranged in a single plane or across two axial planes, we show how these limits scale with the number of traps and SLM pixels, and establish conditions for focusing light in three dimensions. Numerical experiments demonstrate that optimized holograms can closely approach these theoretical limits, suggesting that further improvements in phase optimization alone offer limited power savings. Instead, our results reveal how the choice of illumination and trap geometry can improve light efficiency, providing practical guidelines for designing larger, more power-efficient optical-tweezer arrays.
item.dc:creator: Anzhou Wen, Hengyu Lian, Kevin Yipu Wu, Maxwell F. Parsons, Praneeth Chakravarthula

item.title: Thouless pumping and Haldane-model topology in a driven extended SSH chain
item.description: arXiv:2611.10507v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Thouless pumping provides a powerful route for probing Chern topology through quantized motion in one-dimensional lattices. We investigate such a topological pump in an extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model with tunable next-nearest-neighbor hoppings. A graphical representation in Bloch space is used to construct pumping schemes. In this framework, the Bloch vector traces a closed loop that evolves in time. The Chern number of the synthetic band is then determined by the motion of this loop. Quantum pumping phenomena are demonstrated for a filled band and for a bosonic wave packet driven by Bloch oscillations. We further show that the Haldane model can be mapped to the driven extended SSH chain by replacing a quasimomentum by the pumping time. The quantized charge pump indicates that the Chern number of a two-dimensional model can be read out from a one-dimensional pumping protocol, offering an accessible route for detecting higher-dimensional topology, such as in photonic and cold-atom platforms.
item.dc:creator: Zhen Dong, Xin-Lei Zhao, Yi Zheng

item.title: Integrals of motion for the deformed $W$-algebra $W_{q,t}(D_l)$
item.description: arXiv:2611.10580v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The deformed $W$-algebra $W_{q,t}(D_l)$ of type $D_l$ possesses an infinite family of commuting elements that can be viewed as a two-parameter deformation of the classical Hamiltonians for the KdV hierarchy of type $D_l$; these conserved charges are termed local integrals of motion (IMs). Concurrently, the quantum toroidal algebra $U_q(D_l^{"})$ of type $D_l$ admits four distinct representations via free field realizations, each corresponding to one of the four end nodes of the affine Dynkin diagram. Utilizing these representations, we associate an infinite set of commuting operators with each node, which we define as non-local integrals of motion. Both local and non-local integrals of motion act simultaneously on a shared Fock space consisting of $l+1$ free fields. We provide a direct, computational proof demonstrating that these local and non-local integrals of motion mutually commute.
item.dc:creator: Michio Jimbo, Takeo Kojima

item.title: Markov-Shielded Typicality for Thermal Quantum States
item.description: arXiv:2611.10593v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Pure states of quantum many-body systems at thermal equilibrium are known to be typical, in a sense that a randomly chosen pure state from an appropriate energy shell reproduces the Gibbs-state expectation values of most observables acting on a small subsystem. However, such typical states are intrinsically stochastic, conventionally generated from the random high-temperature state, suffer from statistical fluctuations, and do not provide a continuous connection to the ground state. Here, we introduce a deterministic variational framework for constructing a Markov-Shielded Typical (MST) state, a unique thermal pure-state representative whose local reduced density matrices closely approximate those of the Gibbs state, from the ground state up to infinite-temperature limit. Our approach reformulates free-energy minimization by replacing the nonlocal von Neumann entropy with a local, computationally tractable Markov entropy, where we establish rigorous upper and lower bounds of MST free energy to lie in the very vicinity of the thermal free energy. This framework extends the concept of typicality to deterministic pure-state representations of thermal equilibrium, offering a scalable wave-function approach with potential applications to both classical and quantum computing.
item.dc:creator: Atsushi Iwaki, Chisa Hotta

item.title: A new butterfly in the meadow: magnetic lattice graphs with a circulant vertex coupling
item.description: arXiv:2611.10767v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We analyze the spectrum of quantum square lattice graph exposed to a homogeneous magnetic field with a rational flux through plaquette, assuming all nontrivial cases of the vertex coupling which is circulant and scale-invariant, with a particular attention to those of them that give rise to a dynamics violating the time reversal invariance. Except for two cases with partially decoupled edges, the remaining twelve split into two spectral classes; the second one offers a hitherto unknown butterfly pattern.
item.dc:creator: Pavel Exner, Jan Peka\v{r}

item.title: BP-based qLDPC Decoding under Long-range Correlated Noise: Trapping Configurations and Prior Mismatch
item.description: arXiv:2611.10796v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the robustness of two state-of-the-art BP-based qLDPC decoders, Relay-BP and beam search, designed for independent noise when applied to spatially correlated noise with unchanged single-mechanism error probabilities. We generate correlated errors with a hidden Gaussian Markov random field, which lets us control the strength and range of the correlation while keeping every marginal error probability exact. This setting complements correlation-aware decoding: it asks how existing decoders perform when their assumed joint error model is mismatched. Across multiple tested circuits and code instances that we simulated, we observe that correlations can change logical error rates by orders of magnitude, reduce the finite-size distance advantage, and alter the relative ranking of Relay-BP, beam search, and BP-OSD. On one of the two tested circuits, Relay-BP and beam search become worse than BP-OSD, and increasing relay memory or beam width does not compensate for the degradation. Configuration analysis indicates that correlation primarily increases the probability of trapping configurations that are known to challenge these decoders; at matched error weight, correlated errors still cause decoding failures several times more often than i.i.d. errors. Finally, supplying the decoders with the marginals conditioned on the hidden field recovers most of the lost performance in the tested settings identifying prior mismatch as a major contributor to performance degradation under correlation.
item.dc:creator: Abhinav Dangi, Avhishek Chatterjee

item.title: Spin Asymmetries for Twisted-Neutron Capture by Polarized $^3$He Nuclei
item.description: arXiv:2611.10829v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We provide a theoretical analysis of a nuclear reaction caused by twisted neutrons that carry an additional Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) along the propagation direction. Angular momentum selection rules are derived for the thermal-neutron capture reaction on a spin-polarized $^3$He nucleus. We demonstrate that noticeable novel spin effects due to OAM are limited to the region of the size of de Broglie wavelength around the phase singularity of the beam. Spin asymmetries are predicted for a range of experimental constraints.
item.dc:creator: Rakhee Roy, Carl E. Carlson, Andrei Afanasev

item.title: Qubit representation of the mass observable in quantized Schwarzschild interior
item.description: arXiv:2611.10933v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a quantum-computational framework for the mass observable of the Wheeler--DeWitt quantized Schwarzschild black-hole interior. Working in the physical sector spanned by correlated two-mode oscillator states, we construct finite-dimensional representations of the mass operator and map them onto qubit operators through Pauli decomposition. We analyze the resulting representations for increasing truncation sizes and establish analytically the scaling of the number of nonvanishing Pauli terms and independent measurement settings. These results provide a quantitative characterization of the quantum resources required to encode and measure the black-hole mass observable. As a representative benchmark, we implement a two-qubit variational quantum eigensolver for the smallest nontrivial truncation and find excellent agreement with the exact finite-dimensional spectrum. We further describe a quantum-circuit procedure for verifying the Wheeler--DeWitt constraint independently of the mass estimation. Our results provide a direct connection between Wheeler--DeWitt quantum gravity and quantum computation and establish a structured route toward the quantum simulation of gravitational observables.
item.dc:creator: Babak Vakili

item.title: Imaging spin entanglement with a scanning tunneling microscope
item.description: arXiv:2611.10946v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Artificial spin arrays assembled on surfaces enable atomic-scale studies of quantum correlations. Here we establish a hierarchy of connections between spin inelastic electron tunneling spectroscopy (IETS) and entanglement in spin-$1/2$ systems. We first show that the number of spectroscopically active transitions in a spin-$1/2$ dimer serves as an entanglement witness. Using the leading-order tunneling conductance for the tip placed on spin $i$, $dI(i)/dV$, we then relate spectral moments $\mathcal{M}^{(n)}(i)=\int V^n(d^2I(i)/dV^2)\,dV$ to quantum correlations. The zeroth moment probes the one-tangle in systems with a gapped, nondegenerate ground state. For rotationally invariant Heisenberg systems, the first moment yields thermal spin correlators $\langle\boldsymbol S(i)\cdot\boldsymbol S(j)\rangle$, enabling reconstruction of nearest-neighbor concurrence and spatial imaging of entanglement in spin chains. It also provides access to the internal energy and magnetic specific heat, both usable as entanglement witnesses. Applying this approach to experimental IETS data from nanographene spin chains, we find good agreement with theory. We further discuss how the second moment probes longer-range correlations and the inverse moment relates to local spin susceptibility. For spin-$1/2$ trimers, we connect inter-multiplet inelastic spectral weight to genuine tripartite entanglement quantified by the concurrence fill. Finally, we reconcile the local character of IETS with its sensitivity to nonlocal entanglement through an analogy with digital quantum circuits, where Hamiltonian evolution implements multiqubit operations. These results establish IETS as a tool for quantifying and imaging entanglement in engineered on-surface spin systems.
item.dc:creator: J. C. G. Henriques, B. Vi\~na-Baus\'a, I. Brihuega, J. Fern\'andez-Rossier

item.title: A reachability criterion for spectrally factorable SPDC in coupled waveguides without periodic poling
item.description: arXiv:2611.11086v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Producing spectrally pure photon pairs by spontaneous parametric down-conversion without periodic poling would broaden the choice of nonlinear materials. It requires optical modes that provide both phase matching and suitable group velocities. We derive a joint reachability criterion for a constant-cross-section coupler with a nonlinear main guide and a linear auxiliary. In a two-mode description, phase closure fixes the hybridization parameter that also determines the main-guide participation and the attainable group-delay ratio. This relation screens material and mode pairs and specifies detuning and participation targets for full-vector refinement. A first-order purity map connects the reachable delay ratio and bandwidth--length product to the photon-pair spectrum. A full-vector AlN/TiO$_2$ feasibility example satisfies direct phase matching with a ratio of pump--idler to pump--signal group-delay mismatches of $-0.899$ and yields a calculated unfiltered Schmidt purity of 0.789 over 5 mm. The criterion links phase closure, dispersion control, and nonlinear participation when assessing coupled-waveguide sources beyond periodically poled materials.
item.dc:creator: Qiang Sun, Ke Wang, Andrew D. Greentree

item.title: Coherent Conversion of an Interacting Dark-State-Polariton Condensate into a Photonic Bose-Einstein Condensate
item.description: arXiv:2611.11180v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: An interacting condensate can retain an observable imprint of its preparation after the interactions are switched off. For light, accessing this regime requires separating the formation of a photon condensate from the material medium that redistributes its energy. We investigate a multimode-cavity scheme in which an interacting dark-state-polariton condensate is coherently converted into a confined photonic Bose-Einstein condensate as the atom-cavity coupling is removed. The polariton mass, matter fraction, and particle number control the condensate occupation during preparation. Remarkably, changing the mass also modifies the condensate's response to repulsion through the spatial overlap of its orbitals, even when the entire single-particle spectrum is held fixed. Ideal mode-preserving conversion conserves the full natural-orbital occupation spectrum, while finite-time few-body calculations show that additional occupation changes during transfer are much smaller than those established during interacting preparation. Once decoupled from matter, the photons evolve under the free cavity Hamiltonian while retaining correlations acquired in the interacting gas. Interference between cavity modes produces oscillations in the photon density, while resonant pair correlations persist after interaction removal and distinguish the resulting photon state from a quadratic thermal state with the same one-body density matrix.
item.dc:creator: G. D. de Moraes Neto, M. A. de Ponte, N. G. de Almeida, Miled H. Y. Moussa

item.title: Ergotropy as distance from equilibrium
item.description: arXiv:2611.11343v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that the ergotropy (a.k.a available energy) of a thermally isolated system is the $1$-Wasserstein distance between two energy probability density functions. Specifically, between the energy profile of the system state, and the energy profile of its associated passive state. We prove this for both classical and quantum systems, and illustrate it with examples. Our result formalises the intuition that ergotropy is a quantifier of distance from equilibrium
item.dc:creator: Michele Campisi

item.title: Industrial RPCVD growth of high-purity 28Si epilayers with 29Si content below 30 ppm for high-fidelity electron spin qubits
item.description: arXiv:2611.11405v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Silicon quantum-dot spin qubits are among the most promising routes to large-scale quantum computation, but the residual 29Si nuclear spins in natural silicon impose a hyperfine dephasing limit that must be overcome by isotopic purification. Here, we report the epitaxial growth of high-purity 28Si on float-zone silicon using an industrial reduced-pressure chemical vapor deposition (RPCVD) system. Secondary-ion mass spectrometry (SIMS) confirms an 28Si isotopic purity of 99.997%, with the 29Si concentration below 30 ppm. Through a systematic vacuum annealing matrix (850-1150 C), combined with atomic force microscopy and SIMS, we investigate the defect-mediated decomposition of the native oxide and the injection of non-equilibrium vacancies. We identify a thermal-budget window below 950 C within which the thin-layer structure of 28Si remains intact. At 1.5 K, magnetotransport measurements reveal a peak Hall mobility of 12,858 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1 and a quantum scattering lifetime of 0.659 ps, corresponding to a single-particle level broadening of 499 micro-eV. A double quantum dot fabricated on this platform exhibits a T2* of 0.62 us, a Hahn-echo coherence time of 28.8 us, and single-qubit gate fidelities of up to 99.9% measured by randomized benchmarking. Our results establish industrial RPCVD as a promising route toward high-coherence, high-fidelity silicon spin qubits.
item.dc:creator: Zhenzhen Kong, Weizhu Liao, Ning Chu, Yiwen Zhang, Ying Zhang, Jixuan Li, Changyang Xu, Yongliang Hao, Yi Zhou, Yanpeng Song, Xiaomeng Liu, Hailing Wang, Xiangsheng Wang, Jinbiao Liu, Chao Zhao, Hao Meng, Gang Cao, Guo-Ping Guo, Hai-Ou Li, Guilei Wang

item.title: Solution Size Growth as an Obstacle to Iterative Refinement for Linear Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2611.11419v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Iterative refinement is a technique used to exponentially boost the precision of the solution to certain problems by solving a sequence of related problem instances. We study the size of the solutions arising from the sequence of problems produced by the iterative refinement algorithm when applied to linear optimization problems (LPs). We introduce a class of problems for which the size of such solutions can grow exponentially with the number of refinement iterations, and we show evidence that to avoid this undesirable behavior, a black-box LP solver would have to be \emph{lucky}---a concept introduced formally in this paper, by which we mean that the solver would have to return a solution of better quality than what is required by its termination tolerances. Furthermore, we show that the exponential scaling occurs if one uses a natural instantiation of the simplex algorithm using Bland's pivoting rule. We discuss the implications of our lower bound on the solution size for optimization algorithms whose running time depends polynomially on the solution size, such as quantum multiplicative weights update algorithms and quantum matrix games algorithms.
item.dc:creator: Henry Graven, Giacomo Nannicini

item.title: High-sensitivity sensing technology of 10 MHz radio frequency electric field based on Rydberg atoms
item.description: arXiv:2611.11430v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: To address the pressing need for high-sensitivity, miniaturized electric field sensors in the short-wave communication band (3-30 MHz), this study proposes and demonstrates a radio frequency electric field quantum sensing scheme based on cesium atomic Rydberg states and the electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) effect. The scheme employs an all-infrared optical design, utilizing 852 nm probe light, 1470 nm dressing light, and 780 nm coupling light to efficiently prepare the 49P3/2 Rydberg state in a room-temperature cesium vapor cell, which is then probed non-destructively via ladder-type four-level EIT spectroscopy.
item.dc:creator: Yulong Han, Zhengye Shan, Kan Zhang, Jinfang Sun, Lihua Zhang, Bang Liu, Dongsheng Ding

item.title: Spin entanglement in $pp$ and $pA$ collisions: high-energy TMD effects and fragmentation probes
item.description: arXiv:2611.11568v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Spin-spin correlations of a quark-antiquark pair produced in proton-proton or proton-Ion collisions are investigated in $k_T$-factorization within the shockwave formalism. We construct the full spin-density matrix of both inclusive and diffractive channels in the limit in which the two quarks are back-to-back. In the inclusive channel, due to linearly polarized gluons, we show that a $\cos (2 \phi)$-modulation of the concurrence, stabilizer R\'enyi entropy, and quantum discord emerges and depends on the interplay between six small-$x$ gluon TMDs. The modulation is predicted to be maximally strong and independent of the transverse momentum imbalance, $q$, from a dilute (BFKL) perspective, while it is considerably suppressed by saturation effects. In diffraction, we observe that the pair is always entangled and exhibits the same properties found in diffractive DIS. We explain how these properties follow directly from the exclusive and eikonal nature of the Pomeron exchange. We trace this behavior to a spin-density matrix of rank at most two with maximally mixed marginals. For this class of states, entanglement and Bell nonlocality coincide even when the state is mixed, while the explicit form of the light-front helicity amplitudes ensures that both persist in the whole phase space. We suggest accessing the spin correlations in unpolarized hadron collisions through the Collins and dihadron fragmentation functions. We point out that, in inclusive production, for massless quarks, suitably chosen double-Collins asymmetries provide promising entanglement witnesses.
item.dc:creator: Michael Fucilla

item.title: Comments on: "Optimized thermal control of a dual-wavelength-resonant nonlinear cavity"
item.description: arXiv:2611.11590v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This comment addresses the publication [Appl. Opt. 65, 7090 (2026)] which targets an alleged ``optimization'' of a patented invention conceived by the author. The invention had introduced a multi-temperature management scheme for a dual-wavelength-resonant nonlinear cavity that optimized the crystal temperature around the beam waist for phase-matching, while utilizing independently adjustable temperatures in other regions of the same crystal to simultaneously satisfy the double-resonance condition. A foundational form of this invention was initially utilized by co-author H. Vahlbruch without the author's prior knowledge during the construction of the squeezed-light laser for the Virgo gravitational wave detector. In their publication, the three authors now propose a variant that reduces the maximum achievable temperature differential. Here, I demonstrate that this approach does not constitute an optimization but, on the contrary, represents a regression that dismantles the invention. In general, a high-quality implementation of this invention fundamentally depends on maximizing the achievable temperature differential. Only then can the problematic phase differences---introduced by dielectric coatings, Gouy phase shifts, and suboptimal poling lengths at the crystal facets---be effectively compensated for, particularly in short crystals. If desired, smaller temperature differences can always be selected dynamically anyway.
item.dc:creator: Roman Schnabel

item.title: Lieb-Robinson bound for one-dimensional continuum fermions
item.description: arXiv:2611.11655v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The central difficulty in quantum many-body physics is that the Hilbert space dimension grows exponentially with the total degrees of freedom. A key feature to circumvent this problem is locality, which manifests dynamically through an approximate causal structure in the form of a Lieb-Robinson bound (LRB). LRBs have been proved for quantum spin systems and certain lattice boson systems, but so far never for realistic continuum systems. We present the first LRB that applies to a standard system of one-dimensional continuum fermions. It applies to initial states with controlled moments of local particle number and energy and is thus thermodynamically stable. Our result breaks the main technical barrier that has existed for using the vast locality toolbox on continuum systems.
item.dc:creator: Marius Lemm, Hailun Lu, Harman Preet Singh

item.title: Integer electron-count cuts in variational second-order reduced-density-matrix theory. II. A convergent hierarchy of rigorous relaxations for real-space pair-density representability
item.description: arXiv:2611.11707v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Variational second-order reduced-density-matrix calculations can dissociate molecules into fractionally charged fragments; Part I largely removed this failure with integer electron-count conditions on fixed partitions. Building on the realizability theory of point processes, we place these conditions in a convergent hierarchy of rigorous relaxations, defined by finite occupation linear programs (LPs) on spatial partitions, for real-space pair densities at fixed one-particle density. Every level contains all representable pair densities, the levels tighten under nested refinement, and their intersection characterizes pair densities admitting a symmetric $N$-particle probability-measure extension. In a fixed orbital basis the levels give monotonically increasing lower bounds to the full configuration-interaction energy, which they need not reach, even for the Coulomb repulsion. The spin-summed real-space cuts of Part I are its two-cell members. The LP optimum is also a measure: at fixed one-particle density it equals the $L^1$ distance of the coarse-grained candidate from representability and increases under refinement to that of the candidate, with a vanishing coarse-graining error; its primal law constructs a representable approximation, and its dual a violated valid inequality, used as a cut in molecular calculations. The count conditions are not implied by the usual positivity conditions: moment data that satisfy all three-particle positivity conditions, including $T_1$ and $T_2$, give through Gaussian orbitals a smooth pair density that violates an integer count. For atoms at fractional electron number, ensemble relaxations with the integer-count condition lie closer to the exact piecewise-linear energy than the zero-variance fixed-$N$ form.
item.dc:creator: Maho Nakata

item.title: Proof of the R\'{e}nyi QNEC
item.description: arXiv:2611.11760v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a general proof of the R\'{e}nyi QNEC formulated using the Araki-Masuda weighted $L_p$ norms for all $p > 2$. This generalizes the algebraic proof of the QNEC applicable at $p=2$. Our approach utilizes a weighted version of a conditional $L_p$ norm which extrapolates the quantum expansion/ant-quantity. We elucidate some properties of the corresponding weighted conditional entropy both for half-sided modular inclusions and for general von Neumann subalgebras with a common cyclic and separating vector. The $p=2$ limit computes a conditional dynamical entropy originally defined in the context of black hole dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Faulkner

item.title: Proof of the QNEC, without assumptions and under a weight
item.description: arXiv:2611.11920v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We complete a proof of the quantum null energy condition (QNEC) in the mathematical framework of Half-Sided Translations and Modular Inclusions (HST/HSMI) removing an assumption that applied to previous proofs. Here we establish a theorem, which when translated to a physical setting implies that the relative entropy comparing the state of fields outside a stationary black hole with a Hartle-Hawking (HH) state is always a convex function of the horizon cut. Previous proofs only applied when a purification with finite null energy was available. We also obtain a QNEC generalization in which the HH Hilbert space is replaced with one based on a weight which is plausibly of relevance to evaporating black holes in flat space.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Faulkner

item.title: Semiclassical Asymptotics of Entanglement in Torus-Link States
item.description: arXiv:2611.11961v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the entanglement entropy of topological quantum states associated with $T_{d,\,dn}$ torus links in (2+1)-dimensional SU(2) Chern--Simons theory at level $k$. These links consist of $d$ components with pairwise linking number $n$, and the corresponding link-complement states provide a natural setting to study multipartite entanglement in topological quantum field theories. We analyze the semiclassical limit $k\to\infty$ of the entanglement entropy by deriving the asymptotic behavior of the moments of the reduced density matrix. To achieve this, we decompose the integrable-representation space into left-edge, right-edge, and bulk regions and employ the stationary-phase method to evaluate their respective contributions. We find that the leading asymptotic behavior is governed entirely by the two edge regions, while the bulk contribution is asymptotically suppressed. The resulting expression for the limiting entanglement entropy is given in terms of Hurwitz zeta functions and exhibits a dependence on the residue class of $k$ modulo $n$. We further investigate the dependence of the limiting entanglement entropy on the winding parameter $n$ and the number of link components $d$. In the large-$d$ limit, the entropy reduces to a binary entropy determined by two normalized weights associated with the left and right edges. Finally, we show that the two iterated limits, $k\to\infty$ and $d\to\infty$, commute, reproducing the result obtained previously by taking the large-party limit first.
item.dc:creator: Vikash Ganwariya, Simran Sain, Siddharth Dwivedi

item.title: Rapid high-purity loading of barium ion via relayed selectivity from naturally abundant source
item.description: arXiv:2611.11990v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Trapped ions is one of the promising platforms for realizing quantum information processing and quantum simulation. Selective and rapid loading of a specific isotope lays the critical foundation for such purpose particularly when scaling up the system size. Here we demonstrate a new method for rapid isotope-selective loading of $^{137}\mathrm{Ba}^{+}$ or $^{135}\mathrm{Ba}^{+}$, two types of promising ion qubits, from naturally abundant source using a three-step, ultraviolet-free photoionization scheme. Neutral atoms are selected on the narrow 791 nm $6s^2\,{}^1S_0\rightarrow6s6p\,{}^3P_1^o$ transition, resonantly transferred at 554 nm to $6s6d\,{}^3D_1$, and ionized using an existing 532 nm Raman beam. A spectral-overlap analysis based on isotope and hyperfine shifts shows relayed selectivity that the second step can further suppress undesired-isotope excitation and no contaminant ion is detected during our entire experiment. Besides, the resonant drive of the second step excitation yields a prominent loading rate of the selected species. This strategy using multi-step excitations to establish relayed selectivity can be extended to high-purity loading of other species of ions.
item.dc:creator: Zichun Zhou, Xuhui Yao, Jiaze Li, Yuncheng Xie, Haozhe Shi, Yanxin Liu, Weibin Chu, Lei Feng

item.title: Discrete time crystals stabilized by bounded measurement noise
item.description: arXiv:2611.12400v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Periodically driven clean interacting systems generically heat up, which destroys discrete time-crystalline order. Here we ask whether continuous weak measurement can stabilize such order. We study a long-range interacting spin chain whose local occupation is continuously monitored. Measurements generally induce a transition from volume-law to area-law entanglement. Yet low entanglement alone is not enough: along typical quantum trajectories, the system still reaches a featureless state with no subharmonic response. In contrast, the most-probable trajectory, obtained by suppressing measurement fluctuations, shows robust period doubling. To connect these limits, we introduce a bounded-noise protocol that restricts measurement fluctuations to a finite window. Narrow windows preserve period doubling. Intermediate windows produce coexisting time-crystalline and non-time-crystalline trajectories. Over time, trajectories leave the time-crystalline group one by one, so the order is long lived but finite. Wide windows destroy the order. Our results establish bounded measurement noise, discarding the large-deviation trajectories, as a route to time-crystalline order in clean systems. They also show that the measurement-induced area-law phase is necessary, but not sufficient, for this order.
item.dc:creator: Pallabi Chatterjee, Tanay Nag, Ranjan Modak

item.title: Holonomy, Spectral Topology, and Detailed Balance in Classical and Open Quantum Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.12514v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Band topology and non-Hermitian spectral theory are now applied to mechanical metamaterials, chiral active fluids, stochastic networks, and open quantum systems. We give a tutorial synthesis organized by holonomy and by one question: what can the spectral data of a linear generator reveal about detailed balance? Three holonomies recur: the Berry phase of a band, the Burgers vector of a dislocation (the integrated torsion of the defect geometry), and the cycle affinity of a Markov network (the holonomy of the connection $\ln(W_{ij}/W_{ji})$). We rederive the Chern numbers $C_m=m(\mathrm{sgn}\,\Omega+\mathrm{sgn}\,\nu_o)$ of a compressible odd-viscous fluid and restate the dislocation zero-mode count of Paulose, Chen, and Vitelli as a pairing of integrated torsion with topological polarization. Our central message is that spectral topology can obstruct detailed balance but does not determine the magnitude of dissipation. Detailed balance is self-adjointness in the inner product fixed by the stationary state, so a non-real eigenvalue, an exceptional point (EP), or a nonzero point-gap winding number of a Markov generator rules it out and forces entropy production $\sigma>0$, with $\sigma\ge k_B j^2/D$ for any current, whereas a real, diagonalizable spectrum does not in general certify it. In the Hatano-Nelson ring, which is normal yet has complex spectrum, $\sigma$ sweeps $(0,\infty)$ at fixed winding number. EPs need a separate assessment of the dynamics: with generalized detailed balance including time-reversal parity, an EP is compatible with equilibrium only through time-reversal-odd dynamics, as at critical damping of a Langevin oscillator, whereas an EP of a system with only even variables, such as an odd elastic medium, certifies a nonequilibrium steady state; in both cases $\sigma$ is analytic across the EP. We propose benchtop tests for each statement.
item.dc:creator: Alvan Hunt

item.title: Symanzik Effective Hamiltonian for Lattice Quantum Field Theories
item.description: arXiv:2611.12520v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a framework to construct the Symanzik effective Hamiltonian for lattice quantum field theories directly based on dimensional analysis and symmetries in the Hamiltonian formulation. This allows to classify all operators which can contribute at a given order in the spatial lattice spacing. This list can be reduced using the equations of motion and other identities. We exemplify the framework for $\phi^4$ and pure gauge theory, obtaining results consistent with earlier publications for the case of classical improvement. It provides the means to develop a non-perturbative improvement programme in the Hamiltonian formulation of lattice quantum field theories in the future.
item.dc:creator: Fernanda Steffens, Carsten Urbach

item.title: Topological states in fractals through a self-similar tensor network encoding
item.description: arXiv:2611.12546v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Tensor network methods have been instrumental in addressing exponentially large many-body problems. Most recently, these techniques have also been applied to single-particle tight-binding Hamiltonians, allowing observables to be evaluated on exponentially large lattices. Here, we show that the scale-separated nature of these methods allows for a natural encoding of self-similar structures, such as the Sierpi\'nski gasket, a scale-invariant fractal with Hausdorff dimension $\log 3/\log 2 \approx 1.58$, yielding an exact and compact representation of Hamiltonians on such lattices. Using this encoding, we study a Chern insulator, the flux kagome model, confined to this fractal geometry, and develop methods to investigate its topological states within a tensor network framework. This allows us to reach much higher fractal generations than would otherwise be possible with dense-matrix methods, resolving the density of states of a deep fractal with over 100 million sites. Furthermore, the larger structures allow us to resolve topology in smaller gaps, suggesting that these methods could be instrumental in understanding the interplay between topology and non-integer dimensionality.
item.dc:creator: Zebedeus F. Osseweijer, Jagoda Malag, Jose L. Lado, Tiago V. C. Ant\~ao, Anouar Moustaj

item.title: The finite projective classification of complex spinors via momentum maps
item.description: arXiv:2611.12549v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We describe the projective orbits of complex spinors from the point of view of the momentum map. We treat the irreducible spin modules in odd dimensions 1,3,5,7,9,11 and the half-spin modules in even dimensions 2,4,6,8,10,12,14, which are the only cases with finitely many orbits. In the Clifford--Fock model, we construct representatives as sums of pure basis spinors, and the coefficients are chosen so that the representative is a critical point of the squared norm of the momentum map. The resulting momentum values in a fixed Weyl chamber distinguish the orbits. Completeness follows from Vinberg's theory of graded Lie algebras and stabilizer actions, independently of the classical spinor classifications. We recover the classical counts of 1,1,1,2,3,5 orbits in the odd cases and 1,1,1,2,2,4,9 in the even cases, and compute the projective dimension of every orbit. In dimension fourteen we also determine the closure order of the orbits, using the fact that the minimum of the squared momentum norm increases strictly under degeneration.
item.dc:creator: Bart{\l}omiej Sikorski, Adam Sawicki

item.title: Neutronic Field-Effect Transistor
item.description: arXiv:2611.12651v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Field-effect electronic devices are in widespread use in communication, computing, data storage, and sensing applications. We demonstrate a neutronic field-effect transistor (NFET) that is analogous to the Datta-Das electron spin transistor and atomtronic devices. The NFET is based on a perfect-crystal Mach-Zehnder neutron interferometer with phase shifts applied to the spin and path degrees of freedom.
item.dc:creator: Dusan Sarenac, Charles W. Clark, Owen Lailey, Muhammad Arif, Wangchun Chen, David G. Cory, Michael G. Huber, Joachim Nsofini, Dmitry A. Pushin

item.title: Higher tensor network states in two spatial dimensions: fundamental theorem for open boundary conditions
item.description: arXiv:2611.12658v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a class of two-dimensional tensor network states obtained by categorifying matrix product states. This procedure leads us to consider bond spaces provided by a 2-vector space associated with the 2-cells of the underlying lattice. Tensor network representations are then defined as module categories over the free monoidal category on a monoidal signature encoding the lattice geometry. We prove a fundamental theorem stating that two representations generating the same states with suitable open boundary conditions are equivalent as module categories. Finally, we introduce a notion of 2-injectivity, a categorified analogue of the injectivity condition for matrix product states.
item.dc:creator: Clement Delcamp, Boris Kj{\ae}r

item.title: One-Particle Resonances and Eigenstate Thermalization in Periodic Free-Fermion Lattices
item.description: arXiv:2611.12701v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study eigenstate fluctuations of the particle number in the nearest-neighbour free-fermion model on the periodic cubic lattice $(\mathbb{Z}/L\mathbb{Z})^d$. For every fixed dimension, every particle number, every subvolume, and every normalized energy eigenstate, we prove a bound of order $NL^{d-1}$ for the particle-number variance. The corresponding eigenstate-thermalization estimate is of order $L^{d-1}/(N\eta^2)$ for fluctuations of relative size $\eta$. In particular, at positive particle density the bound decays as the inverse linear size. The proof decomposes the centered particle-number operator according to one-particle energy transfer and treats the zero- and nonzero-transfer components separately. The nonzero-transfer part is controlled by a sharp resonance bound, proved from Mann's theorem on relations among roots of unity, while the zero-transfer part is estimated by a Hilbert-Schmidt argument. These bounds are optimal in every dimension: the maximal nonzero-gap multiplicity has order $L^{d-1}$, and suitable many-body eigenstates realize matching variance lower bounds and show that the concentration bound cannot be improved in estimates uniform in the tolerance parameter.
item.dc:creator: Tristan Benoist, Vojkan Jak\v{s}i\'c, Claude-Alain Pillet, Anna Szczepanek, Cornelia Vogel

item.title: Polynomial-Space Quantum Algorithms from Classical Branching: Colouring, Domination and Monotone Local Search
item.description: arXiv:2611.12714v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give quantum algorithms for exponential-time problems on $n$ vertices or elements, with bounded error, polynomial space and no quantum random access memory. Our results are these. (1) 4-Colouring in quantum time $O(1.3032^n)$, from a polynomial-space branching algorithm with polynomial-space terminal algorithms; with the branching algorithm alone, $O(1.3100^n)$. The previous best bound in this model, to our knowledge, is $O(1.3231^n)$. (2) $k$-Colouring below the previous best bound for $k \in \{5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11\}$ and $13 \le k \le 18$, from $O(1.4518^n)$ for $k = 5$ to $O(1.9233^n)$ for $k = 18$. (3) Dominating Set in $O(1.2235^n)$, against the previous $O(2^{n/2})$, Independent Dominating Set in $O(1.1583^n)$, and Edge Dominating Set and Minimum Maximal Matching in $O(1.1501^n)$. (4) A quantum form of monotone local search: if the extension problem has a backtracking tree with $c^k$ nodes up to polynomial factors, the problem is solved in quantum time $(2 - 1/c)^{n/2}$ up to polynomial factors. This gives Feedback Vertex Set in $O(1.3081^n)$, Subset and Group Feedback Vertex Set in $O(1.3229^n)$, Cluster Vertex Deletion in $O(1.2033^n)$, 3-Hitting Set in $O(1.2405^n)$, Proper Interval Vertex Deletion in $O(1.3541^n)$, Multicut on Trees in $O(1.1647^n)$ and Min-Ones $d$-SAT in $O^*((2-1/d)^{n/2})$. (5) Quantum exponential-time approximations below the quantum exact bounds, such as a 1.1-approximation for Vertex Cover in $O(1.0555^n)$ and for Feedback Vertex Set in $O(1.2161^n)$. The colouring exponents for $k \ge 6$ come from an evaluation of a known reduction recursion, computed in floating point with a margin.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Senge

item.title: Spin Shuttling Through Quantum-Dot Based Chiral Molecular Bridges: Gauge Constraints, Holonomy, and Quantum Gates
item.description: arXiv:2611.12720v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Chiral molecular bridges between silicon quantum dots can provide novel two-qubit entangling resources via the chirality-induced spin-selectivity (CISS) effect. We evaluate this using Makhlin invariants. Modeling a phase-coherent bridge as an $\mathrm{SU}(2)$-valued hopping between two spins, a Schrieffer-Wolff reduction yields a twisted exchange interaction $J \mathbf{S}_1 \cdot \mathbf{R} \mathbf{S}_2$, whose Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya and symmetric anisotropic parts are fixed by a single bridge angle $\alpha$. Using the Kaplan-Shekhtman-Entin-Wohlman-Aharony (KSEA) gauge argument, we prove this interaction is locally equivalent to isotropic exchange; thus, a single chiral bond does not constitute a new entangling class. Breaking this gauge symmetry reveals genuine chiral utility: chiral exchange converts a uniform transverse field into a synthetic gradient, bringing the two-qubit propagator within $7\times10^{-4}$ of the CNOT class in invariant space 4.7 times faster than an equivalent orthogonal gradient. Shuttling a spin through bridges with non-collinear axes implements a non-Abelian $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ holonomy, yielding rotationally non-reciprocal transport and closed-loop geometric gates that suppress dynamical-phase noise to second order. To address the unsettled microscopic origin of CISS, we introduce a unified transport channel combining coherent rotation, a direction-reversing spin filter, and pointer-basis dephasing. This model obeys an exact $\tanh$ composition law for pumped polarization and a closed-form transverse decay law, yielding four observables that experimentally over-determine the bridge's coherent fraction $F_c$. Finally, we quantify silicon-specific hardware constraints, establishing the Landau-Zener valley-adiabaticity window ($E_v \geq 2.1\sqrt{\hbar v}$) and charge-noise limit ($\sigma_J/J \leq 3\%$) required for $99\%$ gate fidelity.

item.title: Universal semiclassical drift velocity of magnetic edge channels
item.description: arXiv:2611.12783v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Magnetic edge channels, arising at the edge of a two-dimensional electron gas in a magnetic field, are topologically protected and propagate unidirectionally along the edge. Their group velocities at the Fermi level, being averaged harmonically, result in drift velocity, which is related to the edge density of states, quantum capacitance, and the velocity of edge magnetoplasmons. Using semiclassical quantization of electron skipping orbits, we show that the drift velocity equals 1/2 of the electron Fermi velocity in the limit of a large number of edge channels crossing the Fermi level. This result, being universal for a hard edge and for isotropic dispersion, is checked numerically for massive electrons and for massless electrons in graphene. The drift velocity at smooth electrostatically defined edges lacks such universality. In the case of anisotropic dispersion, the semiclassical drift velocity at the hard edge reduces to a coordinate-velocity correlation along the cyclotron orbit.
item.dc:creator: Ekaterina R. Sleptsova, Alexey A. Sokolik

item.title: Enhancing valley splitting in Si/SiGe Wiggle Well quantum dots through integrated stressor-gate architectures
item.description: arXiv:2611.12850v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Engineering large and reproducible valley splittings is essential for the scalable operation of silicon spin qubits. In Si/SiGe quantum dot devices, valley splitting arises predominantly from atomic-scale disorder and is therefore inherently random, motivating approaches that introduce a large deterministic contribution. Strain-assisted Wiggle Wells provide a route to deterministic valley splitting by combining an oscillatory Ge concentration in the Si well with shear strain; however, generating the required strain in a manner compatible with large-scale architectures remains a challenge. Here, we propose patterned stressed thin films as a scalable approach for generating shear strain in the quantum well of Si/SiGe quantum dot devices. Finite-element simulations show that compressively stressed TiN films can generate shear strains exceeding 0.1\% at the quantum well, sufficient for deterministic valley splittings of hundreds of $\mu \text{eV}$ in strain-assisted Wiggle Wells. We show that this strain can extend across multiple quantum dots and is maintained in realistic gate geometries, providing a fabrication-compatible approach for scaling deterministic valley splitting to quantum dot arrays.
item.dc:creator: E. S. Joseph, Talise Oh, D. E. Savage, D. S. Stone, DeAnna Campbell, Benjamin D. Woods, Mark Friesen, M. A. Eriksson

item.title: Kerr-athermal baths enhance cooling in quantum refrigerators
item.description: arXiv:2311.10499v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a three-qubit quantum refrigerator, with a three-body interaction enabling cooling of the target qubit, coupled to harmonic oscillator baths prepared in stationary Kerr-athermal states. The reservoir occupation probabilities are specified by a Kerr-type preparation Hamiltonian, while the bath dynamics during operation are harmonic. We show that these reservoirs lower the steady-state temperature of the cold qubit relative to the thermal-bath reference. The improvement of steady-state cooling is distinct from that of the minimum transient temperature, which is not universally enhanced. In a parameter regime where the thermal reference exhibits only transient cold-qubit cooling, the engineered Kerr-athermal baths can produce a steady-state temperature below the initial value. We also investigate the dependence of the steady-state temperature and minimum attainable temperatures on the anharmonicity in the bath state. Analysis of bath-currents reveals lower steady-state temperatures with nearly unchanged coefficients of performance, revealing that reservoir engineering leads to cold-qubit cooling.

item.title: Sample-Efficient Quantum State Tomography for Structured Quantum States in One Dimension
item.description: arXiv:2410.02583v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we answer this fundamental question affirmatively by using a class of informationally complete positive operator-valued measures (IC-POVMs), including symmetric IC-POVMs (SIC-POVMs) and spherical $t$-designs, focusing on sample complexity while not accounting for the implementation complexity of the measurement settings. For SIC-POVMs and spherical 2-designs, we show that the number of state copies to guarantee bounded recovery error of an MPO state with a constrained least-squares estimator depends on the probability distribution of the MPO under the POVM but scales only linearly with $n$ when the distribution is approximately uniform. For general spherical $t$-designs with a sufficiently large $t$, we prove that only a number of state copies proportional to the number of independent parameters in the MPO is sufficient for a guaranteed recovery of any state represented by an MPO. In addition, we establish a sample complexity lower bound based on the Cramer-Rao bound, showing that, for strictly positive definite MPO states and unbiased estimators, a number of state copies proportional to the number of independent parameters in the MPO is also necessary, although the upper and lower bounds do not yet match in their dependence on the target accuracy. Furthermore, we propose a spectral method and a projected gradient descent (PGD) algorithm to solve the constrained least-squares problem, both equipped with rigorous recovery error guarantees.
item.dc:creator: Zhen Qin, Casey Jameson, Alireza Goldar, Michael B. Wakin, Zhexuan Gong, Zhihui Zhu

item.title: Lazy Qubit Reordering for Accelerating Parallel State-Vector-based Quantum Circuit Simulation
item.description: arXiv:2410.04252v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This article proposes two quantum operation scheduling methods for accelerating parallel state-vector-based quantum circuit simulation using multiple graphics processing units (GPUs). The proposed methods reduce all-to-all communication caused by qubit reordering, which can dominate the overhead of parallel simulation. Our out-of-order approach eliminates redundant reorderings by introducing intentional delays in reordering communications such that multiple reorderings can be aggregated into a single reordering. The delays are carefully introduced based on the principles of time-space tiling, or a cache optimization technique for classical computers, which we use to arrange the execution order of quantum operations. Moreover, we develop these methods tailored for two primary procedures in variational quantum eigensolver simulation: quantum state update (QSU) and expectation value computation (EVC). Our QSU simulation takes an advantage of the hierarchical interconnection of GPU systems to avoid slow inter-node communication. On the other hand, our EVC simulation reduces the number of reorderings by diagonalization of Pauli strings. Experimental validation on 32-GPU executions demonstrates acceleration in QSU and EVC$\unicode{x2014}$up to 54$\times$ and 1,657$\times$, respectively$\unicode{x2014}$compared to an inorder-based method. We believe that our out-of-order approach is useful for accelerating large-scale quantum circuit simulations, including QSU and/or EVC that operate qubits in a regular manner.

item.title: Self-correcting qubit in a strongly driven LC resonator
item.description: arXiv:2412.03650v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a device to realize quantum error correction by dissipation. The device generates Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) states as steady states in a single driven LC resonator. The resonator should have impedance above $h/2e^2\approx 12.9\,{\rm k}\Omega$, and should be driven across a Josephson junction with a high-amplitude voltage tone at frequency near-commensurate with the resonator frequency. In this regime, we show that GKP states emerge as steady-states of the resonator; these states encode a qubit protected against phase-space local noise. Low-lying excitations preserve the quantum information and increase the energy proportionally to a measure of the error degree. Thus, quantum error correction of both bit and phase errors can be achieved with dissipative cooling. Our calculations indicate an achievable coherence time of $ 1000 \times$ the resonator photon lifetime at operating temperatures above $100 \, {\rm mK}$. Beyond steady-state quantum error correction, the device supports protected single-qubit Clifford gates and readout with exponential accuracy corrected by the same dissipative mechanism, as well as magic-state preparation above the distillation threshold.

item.title: Certified Lipschitz Bounds for Hybrid Quantum-Classical Decision Models
item.description: arXiv:2503.07992v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study certified upper bounds on Lipschitz constants for hybrid quantum-classical decision models, which combine classical neural-network layers with parameterized quantum circuits. We pair an SDP-based certificate for classical layers with an exact spectral characterization for probability-output quantum models. For hybrid architectures, these componentwise estimates are connected through the encoding maps to obtain a certified composition bound for the complete model. The resulting bounds support sensitivity analyses relevant to robustness, stability, generalization, and fairness.
item.dc:creator: Sajjad Hashemian, Mohammad Saeed Arvenaghi

item.title: Observation of gyroscopic coupling in a non-spinning levitated ferromagnet
item.description: arXiv:2504.13744v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A non-spinning permanent ferromagnet is predicted to behave as a gyroscope at sufficiently low frequencies, which can be seen as a manifestation of gyromagnetism. This yet unexplored regime, conjectured for the first time by Maxwell in 1861, has recently been proposed for ultrasensitive magnetometry and for atomic-like quantum stabilization of a levitated nanomagnet in a static field. Here, we observe signatures of gyroscopic effects in the rotational dynamics of a non-spinning permanent ferromagnet levitated in a superconducting trap. Specifically, we detect spin-rotation coupling between different librational modes, leading to elliptical trajectories, in good agreement with theoretical predictions. From our measurements, we can infer both the intrinsic angular momentum of the levitated magnet and its gyromagnetic $g$-factor.
item.dc:creator: F. Ahrens, A. Vinante

item.title: Affine Equivalence in the Clifford Hierarchy
item.description: arXiv:2507.14370v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we prove a collection of results on the structure of permutations in the Clifford Hierarchy. First, we leverage results from the cryptography literature on affine equivalence classes of 4-bit permutations which we use to find all 4-qubit permutations in the Clifford Hierarchy. We then use the classification of 4-qubit permutations and previous results on the structure of diagonal gates in the Clifford Hierarchy to prove that all 4-qubit gates in the third level of the Clifford Hierarchy are semi-Clifford. We then leverage results from \cite{He2024} to prove that all 5-qubit gates in the third level of the Clifford Hierarchy are semi-Clifford. We introduce the formalism of cycle structures to permutations in the Clifford Hierarchy and prove a general structure theorem about them, and classify many small cycle structures up to affine equivalence. Interestingly, this classification is independent of the number of qubits. Additionally, we show that all 1-wire-mismatch permutations are in the Clifford Hierarchy.
item.dc:creator: Jonas T. Anderson, Andrew Connelly, Mason Lovejoy-Johnson

item.title: Entanglement sharing schemes
item.description: arXiv:2509.21462v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We ask how quantum correlations can be distributed among many subsystems. To address this, we define entanglement sharing schemes (ESS) where certain pairs of subsystems allow entanglement to be recovered via local operations, while other pairs must not. ESS schemes come in two variants, one where the partner system with which entanglement should be prepared is known, and one where it is not. In the case of known partners, we fully characterize the access structures realizable for ESS when using stabilizer states, and construct efficient schemes for threshold access structures, and give a conjecture for the access structures realizable with general states. In the unknown partner case, we again give a complete characterization in the stabilizer setting, additionally give a complete characterization of the case where there are no restrictions on unauthorized pairs, and we prove a set of necessary conditions on general schemes which we conjecture are also sufficient. Finally, we give an application of the theory of entanglement sharing to resolve an open problem related to the distribution of entanglement in response to time-sensitive requests in quantum networks.

item.title: Ultrafast Meissner-Levitated Microrotor
item.description: arXiv:2509.24964v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Levitated mechanical systems offer a unique and flexible platform for the realization of ultralow noise sensors and tests of fundamental physics. Here, we report the demonstration of a levitated microrotor, consisting of a magnetic microsphere levitated by the Meissner effect at 4.2 K. The rotor reaches rotation frequencies above 2.3 MHz (138 million rpm) while exhibiting an exceptionally low damping rate 4.75 $\times$10$^{-7}$ Hz. Exploiting the linear dependence of friction on the gas density, we demonstrate high-accuracy absolute pressure sensing over a wide range at cryogenic temperature. Finally, we detect the thermal torque noise at intermediate pressure by operating the rotor in synchronized mode, resulting in a first preliminary narrowband search for axion-like dark matter. More broadly, the unique combination of high rotational speed, low temperature, and low thermal torque noise establishes a new regime for precision measurements, with direct implications for the detection of extremely weak forces and fields.
